By Jenny Coleman North West Published 1 hour ago The funeral of rugby league legend Sir Billy Boston will take place later. Boston, who was the first player in rugby league's 130-year history to receive a knighthood, died last month aged 92. His funeral will take place at Wigan Warriors' Brick Community Stadium at 12:30 BST, with a limited number of supporters able to attend. Before the service, a cortege will travel through Wigan , external and arrive at the stadium. The West Stand will be open as Sir Billy makes his final journey through the Stadium Tunnel. A private burial will follow. To play this video you need to enable JavaScript in your browser. This video can not be played Figure caption, Boston is regarded as one of Britain's truly great rugby league players At the request of the Boston family, people attending are being encouraged to wear traditional funeral attire, but items of Wigan Warriors' cherry red can be worn such as scarves, ties and headwear. People are welcome to pay their respects to the funeral cortege, which will follow a route through Wigan. Born in Cardiff in 1934, Boston grew up playing union but was overlooked by his home club. He came to the attention of rugby league scouts while on national service in the north of England, signing for Wigan in 1953 as a 19-year-old. He was picked for the 1954 Great Britain side and was the first black British player to tour Australia and New Zealand. He reached the 100-try milestone in just 68 matches and claimed 478 tries in 488 games for Wigan, helping them win three Challenge Cups and the Championship. It will be part of the £100m CyanLines plan to create a 100-mile (161km) network of walkways around the Greater Manchester region over the next decade. The recently announced route will see the Etihad campus - home to Manchester City FC - connected to Piccadilly station, taking in Ashton Canal, New Islington and Holt Town. Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig said: "It's not just about travel, the whole point of CyanLines is 100 miles of nature connected together, and yes it's about how you move, cycle and walk, but it's something more fundamental." There are two further CyanLines routes in development in Newton Heath and Rusholme. Backing for the plans comes from the Manchester and Trafford councils, the Greater Manchester Combined Authority, Manchester City FC, the Canal and River Trust, property developers Renaker and Urban Splash, and the National Trust, among others. Pete Bradshaw, director of sustainability at Manchester City, said: "The plans for the CyanLines route add a new layer of nature-rich, innovative and imaginative active travel and community experiences for fans, visitors and those living and working in the neighbourhood." Image caption, The next phase of the Castlefield Viaduct park project has also been announced Funding for the next phase of the Castlefield Viaduct "garden in the sky" was also announced. title: Oldham Council condemns attacks on bin crews and traffic wardens

evidence_packet.title: Oldham Council condemns attacks on bin crews and traffic wardens
evidence_packet.lead: A bin wagon had a brick thrown through a side window while out on its rounds in Oldham
evidence_packet.summary: A bin wagon had a brick thrown through a side window while out on its rounds in Oldham
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Council condemns attacks on bin crews and traffic wardens - BBC News Image source, LDRS Image caption, A bin wagon had a brick thrown through a side window while out on its rounds in Oldham By Ed Barnes Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 9 September 2026 Targeting bin crews and traffic wardens out doing their jobs is "unacceptable", a council has said, after a wagon had a brick thrown through its window while out on its rounds. At least one traffic warden was also said to have been targeted in the Goldwick area, Oldham Council said. Speaking after the bin wagon incident last month, a spokesperson said the wagon had its driver-side window smashed "by a resident" and a parking enforcement officer was subjected to abuse. "Our staff are working hard every day to deliver essential services for communities across the borough. These unacceptable actions not only put people at risk but also delay services for other residents," they added. The council has recently laid fresh double yellow lines and given out 273 parking fines so far this year in parts of the Waterloo Street area. "Enforcement officers are carrying out their duties to help keep our highways safe and accessible," the council continued. "Any form of verbal or physical abuse towards our staff is completely unacceptable and will not be tolerated." evidence_packet.evidence_text: Ashton-under-Lyne queen bee killed in hive vandalism - BBC News Image source, Chris Place Image caption, Chris said bricks and wooden poles appeared to have been used to lever the hive over By Haider Saleem Reporting from North West Published 9 September 2026 A queen bee was killed when vandals damaged a community hive that had been set up on a playing field. Chris Place, 74, said bricks and wooden poles appeared to have been used to lever over the hive at King George V Playing Fields in Ashton-under-Lyne, Greater Manchester. He said volunteers had spent the past year growing the thriving colony, but were now having to try to introduce a replacement queen. Volunteers said the damage happened between 17:30 BST on 5 September and 08:30 the following morning. Place, a volunteer beekeeper, said the hive's metal stand was buried about 18in (46cm) into the ground but appeared to have been levered upwards using bricks and wooden poles. Branches had also been taken from a nearby dead hedge and used to strike the hives, he said. Image caption, About seven regular volunteers help care for the bees at the community apiary Place added: "People might think it's just a wooden box that's been knocked over. It isn't. It's a living colony containing thousands of bees." He said an inspection afterwards found the queen was missing and the bees had begun producing queen cells, which indicated the colony had become queenless. Image source, Chris Place Image caption, The damaged hive contained a colony of thousands of bees Place said he had found a replacement queen costing about £50, which volunteers would carefully introduce to the colony. evidence_packet.evidence_text: A woman who falsely accused 10 men of raping her has had her prison sentence increased by two-and-a-half years after the Court of Appeal ruled her original term was "unduly lenient" Stacey Sharples, 31, made false reports causing men to be held in custody at police stations, lose jobs and relationships, and be separated from their children She met the men from Greater Manchester on Facebook and dating apps Plenty of Fish and Badoo between 2013 and 2019, when she was aged between 18 and 24 Sharples, who admitted 10 counts of perverting the course of justice, was originally jailed for four-and-a-half years, but judges increased the term to seven years The Attorney General had referred the sentence to the Court of Appeal, after Sharples was jailed at Bolton Crown Court in March An estimated 264 hours of police time and about £50,000 were wasted in months-long investigations, the court heard

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A strike involving operating theatre staff at four Greater Manchester hospitals has been called off after NHS bosses agreed to fresh talks The UNISON union said the strike by more than 350 workers planned for Monday 14 September will not go ahead after discussions with the Northern Care Alliance NHS Foundation Trust (NCA) However, it said workers - including nurses, clinical support workers and housekeepers - will still walk out on Tuesday and Thursday next week unless there is "significant progress" The NCA said it was "committed to constructive discussions" and had agreed to a meeting with UNISON on Friday, but had "contingency plans" in the event of strikes The strikes, which relate to a dispute around overtime payments, are due to take place at Salford Royal Hospital, Royal Oldham Hospital, Rochdale Infirmary and Fairfield General Hospital in Bury They follow previous strikes in June and August

evidence_packet.summary: The creator and writer of a film documenting last year's Oasis reunion tour has said he hoped it would encourage others to resolve family feuds like the Gallagher brothers Steven Knight said Oasis: Don't Look Back In Anger - which charts their emotional reconciliation after 15 ye
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The creator and writer of a film documenting last year's Oasis reunion tour has said he hoped it would encourage others to resolve family feuds like the Gallagher brothers Steven Knight said Oasis: Don't Look Back In Anger - which charts their emotional reconciliation after 15 years - was "incredibly emotional" and had resonated with many people The Peaky Blinders writer said the reaction to the candid film - which shows "real emotions from real people" - had been "extraordinary", adding: "When you write fiction you aspire to having these kind of reactions." He said if it inspired people to get in touch with family members they have not spoken to for years "then I'm all for it - it's great" The project is part concert film and part documentary and charts the Manchester band on their reunion world tour, which kicked off in Cardiff in July last year It also features the first joint interviews with Noel and Liam in more than 20 years

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A queen bee was killed when vandals damaged a community hive that had been set up on a playing field Chris Place, 74, said bricks and wooden poles appeared to have been used to lever over the hive at King George V Playing Fields in Ashton-under-Lyne, Greater Manchester He said volunteers had spent the past year growing the thriving colony, but were now having to try to introduce a replacement queen Volunteers said the damage happened between 17:30 BST on 5 September and 08:30 the following morning Place, a volunteer beekeeper, said the hive's metal stand was buried about 18in (46cm) into the ground but appeared to have been levered upwards using bricks and wooden poles Branches had also been taken from a nearby dead hedge and used to strike the hives, he said

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Royal hospital Girl, 13, born without hair 'left in tears' after being stripped of funding at Salford Royal "We live in a cruel world, and people stare and say things" Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer and Camilla Foster PA Real Lif A mum said she was left in tears after discovering she could no longer afford specialist wigs for her daughter, who was born without hair Ceri Williams said her 13 year old daughter Kizzi-Rae's hair "grows like fluff and then disappears", and has been receiving vouchers that fully covered the cost of two specialist wigs per year – worth £1,250 each – since she was three years old However, she recently received a letter telling her that because Kizzi-Rae has now been referred back to Wrexham Maelor Hospital from Salford Royal, she is now only entitled to two £100 vouchers a year, leaving the family £2,300 out of pocket A spokesperson from the Northern Care Alliance NHS Foundation Trust, which operates Salford Royal hospital , explained the decision followed a review of the service that led to patients living outside the local area being transitioned to their local healthcare providers "When I first received the letter I cried. evidence_packet.lead: Oldham New arena and thousands of new homes in 'rocketbooster' plan for Oldham Town hall bosses are keen to stress the impact will be felt across the borough with promises of major investment Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 06:12, A new ‘rocketbooster’ could
evidence_packet.summary: Oldham New arena and thousands of new homes in 'rocketbooster' plan for Oldham Town hall bosses are keen to stress the impact will be felt across the borough with promises of major investment Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 06:12, A new ‘rocketbooster’ could
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham New arena and thousands of new homes in 'rocketbooster' plan for Oldham Town hall bosses are keen to stress the impact will be felt across the borough with promises of major investment Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 06:12, A new ‘rocketbooster’ could turbo-charge major changes in Oldham over the next decade. This could see a new indoor arena built, thousands of new homes, and millions of pounds of investment Earlier this week, leaders of Oldham ’s various political parties gave the thumbs up for the creation of a Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC ), a partnership between Oldham council and the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) that will look to fuel further growth in th Those plans have also now been backed by Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig , subject to GMCA approval later this month The MDC in Oldham has been modelled off the one created in Stockport which is regarded as a blueprint for delivering town centre regeneration in the UK . The council leader there Coun Mark Roberts recently described the MDC as a ‘rocketbooster’ that has driven investment forward, If approved by the GMCA, the proposed MDC for Oldham will go to the UK Government and Parliament for approval. If everything goes according to plan, Oldham council hopes to set up the MDC in early 2027

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Once ruled by Romans, a forgotten corner of Oldham has been transformed into UK first Ahead of an opening next week, people have been given a first glimpse at a major new visitor attraction in Oldham Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy A major project ‘unlike anything else in the UK’ is about to open in the heart of Oldham after nearly £13m was spent transforming the area The whole Northern Roots site covers around 160 acres to the south of Oldham town centre next to Alexandra Park. Part of the site was once an old Roman road, the Brook Mill used to dominate the area, and for around five decades, it was used for landfill Now it is entering a new chapter of its history with the area’s new urban farm, considered the largest in the UK , preparing to open its doors next week on September 19 for the first time. The project has been about five years in the making and the Manchester Evening News was giv People will enter through a woodland walkway lit during the darker winter months where people can ‘leave the world behind them and have this really magical experience’. The woodland then opens out into a large green space with views of the Peak District and the urban farm at the A large visitor centre which will offer meeting spaces, a café run by acclaimed chef Mary-Ellen McTague , a large play area, as well as the urban farm itself. There will also be a forestry skills centre on site

The unknown man smashed a window before Lynam poured petrol inside. An ‘explosion’ was caused and the pair fled Lynam was caught after DNA from a balaclava which he discarded nearby was traced to him. evidence_packet.lead: Bolton Plans advance on £520M scheme to build homes and employment space on 700 acres close to Bolton hospital Partners behind the scheme said ‘no comparable site in Greater Manchester offers the same combination of hospital adjacency, medical school An agreement has been signed
evidence_packet.summary: Bolton Plans advance on £520M scheme to build homes and employment space on 700 acres close to Bolton hospital Partners behind the scheme said ‘no comparable site in Greater Manchester offers the same combination of hospital adjacency, medical school An agreement has been signed
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Plans advance on £520M scheme to build homes and employment space on 700 acres close to Bolton hospital Partners behind the scheme said ‘no comparable site in Greater Manchester offers the same combination of hospital adjacency, medical school An agreement has been signed by partners hoping to bring forward a massive development which would ‘create a new neighbourhood’ and transform much of the south of Bolton A partnership agreement has been agreed between organisations including Bolton council, Peel Land and the borough’s NHS trust to move forward the Health Innovation Bolton (HIB) initiative which would have a capital investment of £520M The group described it as a £1 billion catalyst project which ‘puts health and wellbeing at the heart of a 700-acre economic and community development’ The scheme includes 200,000 sqm of employment, R&D and health floorspace alongside more than 2,000 new homes Bolton’s council leader Akhtar Zaman described the huge project as ‘an ideal fit for Bolton’s ongoing regeneration’

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Woman who falsely accused 10 men of raping her has prison sentence increased Court of Appeal judges ruled her original term was 'unduly lenient' News PA and Paul Britton Reporter 15:13, 09 Sep 2026 Updated 15:21, 09 Sep 2026 View Image Stacey S A mother who falsely accused 10 men of raping her has had her prison sentence increased by two-and-a-half years after Court of Appeal judges ruled her original term was 'unduly lenient' Stacey Sharples, 31, from Farnworth in Bolton , made false reports causing men to be held in custody at police stations, lose jobs and partners, and be separated from their children She met the men from Greater Manchester on Facebook and dating apps Plenty of Fish and Badoo between 2013 and 2019 when she was aged between 18 and 24. Sharples admitted 10 counts of perverting the course of justice at Bolton Crown Court in March and was jailed for four-and-a-hal The Attorney General referred the sentence to the Court of Appeal and on Wednesday judges increased the term to seven years. An estimated 264 hours of police time and around £50,000 were wasted in months-long investigations, the court heard Sharples repeated her allegations in lengthy video-recorded interviews but police found many inconsistencies in her accounts

Tributes poured in for 'The Hitman' after the former world champion boxer was found dead at his Hyde home on September 14 last year Fans lined the streets of Tameside and Manchester to say a final farewell to the boxing hero ahead of his funeral the following month. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham New arena and thousands of new homes in 'rocketbooster' plan for Oldham Town hall bosses are keen to stress the impact will be felt across the borough with promises of major investment Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 06:12, A new ‘rocketbooster’ could turbo-charge major changes in Oldham over the next decade. This could see a new indoor arena built, thousands of new homes, and millions of pounds of investment Earlier this week, leaders of Oldham ’s various political parties gave the thumbs up for the creation of a Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC ), a partnership between Oldham council and the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) that will look to fuel further growth in th Those plans have also now been backed by Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig , subject to GMCA approval later this month The MDC in Oldham has been modelled off the one created in Stockport which is regarded as a blueprint for delivering town centre regeneration in the UK . The council leader there Coun Mark Roberts recently described the MDC as a ‘rocketbooster’ that has driven investment forward, If approved by the GMCA, the proposed MDC for Oldham will go to the UK Government and Parliament for approval. If everything goes according to plan, Oldham council hopes to set up the MDC in early 2027

The force's Chief Constable, Sir Stephen Watson, ruled Masood Meah would have been sacked over his actions had he not already resigned as a constable A misconduct hearing took place at GMP headquarters on July 14, with Sir Stephen's ruling now published In it, he said former PC Meah first came into contact with the woman during the course of his duties. He was said to have actively 'followed' and submitted 'commentary and emojis' relating to the woman on social media over a 'protracted period' Mr Meah was warned off by a friend of hers, but the ruling says he 'continued to engage' and responses to her posts 'included various emojis and commentary which can only be interpreted as intimately familiar and designed to flatter' Sir Stephen said he found that in his view, the former officer was 'apparently seeking or encouraging some form of emotional or sexual relationship with a highly vulnerable person'

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Once ruled by Romans, a forgotten corner of Oldham has been transformed into UK first Ahead of an opening next week, people have been given a first glimpse at a major new visitor attraction in Oldham Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy A major project ‘unlike anything else in the UK’ is about to open in the heart of Oldham after nearly £13m was spent transforming the area The whole Northern Roots site covers around 160 acres to the south of Oldham town centre next to Alexandra Park. Part of the site was once an old Roman road, the Brook Mill used to dominate the area, and for around five decades, it was used for landfill Now it is entering a new chapter of its history with the area’s new urban farm, considered the largest in the UK , preparing to open its doors next week on September 19 for the first time. The project has been about five years in the making and the Manchester Evening News was giv People will enter through a woodland walkway lit during the darker winter months where people can ‘leave the world behind them and have this really magical experience’. The woodland then opens out into a large green space with views of the Peak District and the urban farm at the A large visitor centre which will offer meeting spaces, a café run by acclaimed chef Mary-Ellen McTague , a large play area, as well as the urban farm itself. There will also be a forestry skills centre on site

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Oldham Reform boss says he's still in charge despite claims he is being replaced Multiple town hall sources have told the Manchester Evening News Oldham council’s Reform UK group is looking to elect a new leader and other party leaders were rep Oldham Reform’s boss says claims he is no longer in the post are ‘just gossip and hearsay’. This comes two days after other party leaders were reportedly told Councillor Lewis Quigg was being replaced Multiple town hall sources have told the Manchester Evening News Oldham council’s Reform UK group is looking to elect a new leader in the borough. However, Coun Quigg has denied the claims, initially telling the Manchester Evening News he would not ‘confirm nor deny silly allegat He later said the claims are ‘just nonsense really’ and ‘just gossip and hearsay’. When asked to confirm whether he was still leader on September 9, Coun Quigg said: “Clearly.” Coun Quigg has led the borough’s 16-strong group of councillors since he joined Reform in September 2025 and Reform are now second behind Labour in terms of numbers. He has consistently argued his party has the mandate to run the local authority based on strong election results b This week, town hall sources have told the Manchester Evening News Coun Quigg’s deputy Mark Wilkinson has taken over on an interim basis while a new leader is selected over the coming weeks

But they were woken up shortly after by a ‘loud crash’. Mr Marsden went to investigate and found a large fire in their rented end-of-terrace home in Bury He and his wife were able to escape the blaze, but their house was severely damaged and nine months on, remains uninhabitable. Their children had been staying elsewhere for the night Police recovered footage which showed Jody Lynam and a second, unknown offender approaching the house, at about 1.40am on January 18 this year. The unknown man smashed a window before Lynam poured petrol inside. An ‘explosion’ was caused and the pair fled Lynam was caught after DNA from a balaclava which he discarded nearby was traced to him. evidence_packet.summary: Bolton Plans advance on £520M scheme to build homes and employment space on 700 acres close to Bolton hospital Partners behind the scheme said ‘no comparable site in Greater Manchester offers the same combination of hospital adjacency, medical school An agreement has been signed
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Plans advance on £520M scheme to build homes and employment space on 700 acres close to Bolton hospital Partners behind the scheme said ‘no comparable site in Greater Manchester offers the same combination of hospital adjacency, medical school An agreement has been signed by partners hoping to bring forward a massive development which would ‘create a new neighbourhood’ and transform much of the south of Bolton A partnership agreement has been agreed between organisations including Bolton council, Peel Land and the borough’s NHS trust to move forward the Health Innovation Bolton (HIB) initiative which would have a capital investment of £520M The group described it as a £1 billion catalyst project which ‘puts health and wellbeing at the heart of a 700-acre economic and community development’ The scheme includes 200,000 sqm of employment, R&D and health floorspace alongside more than 2,000 new homes Bolton’s council leader Akhtar Zaman described the huge project as ‘an ideal fit for Bolton’s ongoing regeneration’

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Woman who falsely accused 10 men of raping her has prison sentence increased Court of Appeal judges ruled her original term was 'unduly lenient' News PA and Paul Britton Reporter 15:13, 09 Sep 2026 Updated 15:21, 09 Sep 2026 View Image Stacey S A mother who falsely accused 10 men of raping her has had her prison sentence increased by two-and-a-half years after Court of Appeal judges ruled her original term was 'unduly lenient' Stacey Sharples, 31, from Farnworth in Bolton , made false reports causing men to be held in custody at police stations, lose jobs and partners, and be separated from their children She met the men from Greater Manchester on Facebook and dating apps Plenty of Fish and Badoo between 2013 and 2019 when she was aged between 18 and 24. Sharples admitted 10 counts of perverting the course of justice at Bolton Crown Court in March and was jailed for four-and-a-hal The Attorney General referred the sentence to the Court of Appeal and on Wednesday judges increased the term to seven years. An estimated 264 hours of police time and around £50,000 were wasted in months-long investigations, the court heard Sharples repeated her allegations in lengthy video-recorded interviews but police found many inconsistencies in her accounts

Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

evidence_packet.evidence_text: It will be officially opened later this month Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Bowdon's new pitch Bowdon Hockey Club has completed a new pitch two weeks ahead of schedule after 160 individuals and families contributed more than £51,000 towards its replacement The previous surface had been used for hockey and other sports for 25 years and had reached the end of its life. An official opening will take place on Saturday September 26th, with visitors invited to enjoy a day of hockey and family activities The club established a working party to research playing surfaces, suppliers and prices, and the replacement had to be completed during the close season and ready before the end of August for the 2026/27 campaign The project finished two weeks early, allowing players to begin using the new surface ahead of the season Alongside donations from members and supporters, Sport England provided £15,000 in matched funding and supported the financing through a loan scheme. Members also helped through the club’s own loan scheme

evidence_packet.summary: Stacey Sharples, 31, made false reports causing men to be held in custody at police stations, lose jobs and relationships, and be separated from their children She met the men from Greater Manchester on Facebook and dating apps Plenty of Fish and Badoo between 2013 and 2019, when
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stacey Sharples, 31, made false reports causing men to be held in custody at police stations, lose jobs and relationships, and be separated from their children She met the men from Greater Manchester on Facebook and dating apps Plenty of Fish and Badoo between 2013 and 2019, when she was aged between 18 and 24 Sharples, who admitted 10 counts of perverting the course of justice, was originally jailed for four-and-a-half years, but judges increased the term to seven years The Attorney General had referred the sentence to the Court of Appeal, after Sharples was jailed at Bolton Crown Court in March An estimated 264 hours of police time and about £50,000 were wasted in months-long investigations, the court heard Sharples repeated her allegations in lengthy video-recorded interviews but police found many inconsistencies in her accounts

evidence_packet.lead: Oldham Council has secured a court order requiring the removal of an unauthorised encampment from Oldham Edge
evidence_packet.summary: Oldham Council has secured a court order requiring the removal of an unauthorised encampment from Oldham Edge
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Council has secured a court order requiring the removal of an unauthorised encampment from Oldham Edge Council officers first visited the site on Thursday 6th August following concerns from residents and people using the park. Officers spoke to those at the encampment, who said they intended to leave by Saturday 8th August As the site had not been vacated, the Council returned with support from Greater Manchester Police on Tuesday 11th August. A formal direction was served under Section 77 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994, requiring those at the encampment to leave and remove their The Council also provided information about authorised sites in Greater Manchester, along with advice about health, wellbeing and reporting hate crime After the direction was not followed, the Council began court proceedings. On Monday 17th August, Tameside Magistrates’ Court granted an order requiring the removal of the encampment The site was vacated later that day. A significant amount of waste was left behind, which has now been removed by the Council’s cleansing team

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Thirteen local artists, schools, charities and community groups have been chosen to bring their ideas to life during Oldham’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture From theatre, film and music to a new mural and giant fuzzy felt artwork, the projects cover a wide range of art forms and celebrate Oldham’s people, places and stories Oldham secured the Town of Culture title with its programme, Rising Up . evidence_packet.evidence_text: A new ‘trainer flat’ which gives cared for young people a taste of what it is like to live independently has been opened by Rochdale Borough Council Living alone for the first time can be a daunting experience, but it can be an even greater challenge for those who have grown up in care as some may only have a limited support network that they can rely on This can make adjusting to new responsibilities such as paying utility bills, managing a tenancy agreement, budgeting and keeping on top of household chores harder However, through the help of the local authority’s trainer flat scheme, of which there are now 14 across the borough, cared for young people aged 17 and over are being offered the perfect stepping stone to safely prepare for life on their own Fully furnished and equipped with everyday household goods, these flats provide young people with the time and support they need to develop the knowledge, skills and confidence to successfully transition into adulthood This support is offered without the financial pressures normally associated with setting up a home, with the young people not required to contribute towards gas, electricity, water and other property-related utility costs until they turn 18

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Child safe travel scheme adds another school – Bolton Council Published: Wednesday, 9th Sep 2026 Another Bolton primary school is set to join the growing number that are making it safer and easier for children to walk, bike or wheel to school. The Ferns Primary Academy on Plodder Lane will start operating Schools Streets from Monday, September 14. It means that on days when the school is open, access to Westend Street will be controlled at school drop off and pick up times. Residents, workers, school staff and emergency responders will still be able to get in and out of the street, with school staff and trained volunteers on hand to let the necessary vehicles through. Controlled access will operate in the morning from 8:20am to 9:00am, and in the afternoon from 2:30pm to 3:15pm. This latest School Streets project brings the total operating in Bolton to five, with four starting earlier this year. More widely, the number of Schools Streets across Greater Manchester has reached over 40, while London has over 700. In Bolton, School Streets are in place at: Kearsley West Primary School St. Bedes Primary Academy Sharples Primary School The Gates Primary School The Ferns Primary School Before bringing in School Streets the schools trialled them for a day, with feedback from parents, residents and children up to 90 per cent positive. Among the most common reasons were better safety for the children and a calmer environment during school opening time. Across the UK, travelling to and from school is the most dangerous time of day for road accidents involving children, with almost three-quarters of accidents happening between 8am and 9am and 3pm and 7pm. evidence_packet.evidence_text: A shop in Leigh town centre has been closed for three months following repeated seizures of illicit tobacco products Wigan Council’s Trading Standards team, in partnership with Greater Manchester Police, secured the closure order for Shop & Save on Bradshawgate after concerns were raised about illegal sales Following an investigation by Trading Standards, a three-month closure order was approved at Wigan and Leigh Magistrates Court on Thursday, 3rd September Councillor Kevin Anderson, portfolio holder for police, crime and civil contingencies said: "This closure order yet again demonstrates our commitment to tackling illegal trading and protecting our communities across Wigan Borough “Traders who engage in this kind of activity will not be allowed to continue breaking the law, and we will continue working with partners to investigate reports of illicit sales and take robust action where unlawful activity is identified.” Over the course of two months, Trading Standards officers seized 7,380 sticks of illicit cigarettes and four kilograms of illicit hand rolling tobacco, which was concealed in elaborate hides within the premises

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Leisure centre memberships in Wigan Borough have reached never-before-seen heights as residents become more active A strong summer of sign-ups has seen the council-run Be Well brand surpass 20,000 members for the first time ever - suggesting local people are increasingly conscious of the importance of moving more Memberships are up by just shy of 2,000 this year alone and have close to doubled since the council’s decision to bring leisure services back in-house in 2021 Total visitor numbers across Be Well’s seven sites also continue to rise, putting them on course to top the 1.73million visits that were made by residents from April 2025 to March 2026 The impressive figures come on the back of major council investment in the borough’s leisure facilities, with recent refurbs bringing brand-new, state-of-the-art fitness equipment at all locations Councillor Chris Ready, Wigan Council’s cabinet portfolio holder for communities and neighbourhoods, believes a combination of cutting-edge facilities, an inclusive community, and an emphasis on holistic wellbeing over body image has been the secret to Be Well’s success

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.evidence_text: GRUB on the Docks is bringing the flavour this summer – think unreal street food, ice-cold drinks and non-stop vibes right in the MediaCity gardens, on the waterfront We’re talking a stacked rotation of indie food like Sizzling Seoul, Umami Cartel, Oppa Korean Dogs and more, switching it up every week so there’s always something new to try Midweek just got better. Every Wednesday, buy two glasses of the same wine and we’ll top up the rest of the bottle on us. No catch, no fuss just a proper reason to make Wednesday your new favourite day Clock off and head straight to the water’s edge. It’s been a pleasure to have them with us. It already has a strong tech base and devolution gives us a chance to align policy, funding and delivery more closely with what is happening on the ground To do that well, Combined Authorities and others need to understand that ecosystems are much broader and deeper than most public-facing institutions realise, that matters if they are going to make good decisions on skills, infrastructure, procurement and innovation support AI and emerging technologies clearly need focus because their impact will be felt across every part of the economy, but policy needs to keep pace with how those technologies are being used by businesses. Government and Combined Authorities will have more impact if they understand The new Digital Campus in Manchester is a good example of where this could become practical; a larger concentration of public sector digital capability in Manchester should create new routes for startups and scaleups to work with the government. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Events EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters Official Chamber Post FREE Online Thursday 10 Sep 10am - 11am Book Now About the event The way low-value goods enter the European Union is changing From 1 July 2026, the EU introduced a new €3 customs duty on low-value consignments valued up to €150 entering the EU from outside the bloc. The change removes the previous duty exemption and introduces new considerations for businesses exporting goods directly to EU customers The new duty applies based on product categories/tariff classifications rather than simply per parcel, meaning shipments containing different types of goods could face multiple charges. For example, a parcel containing products under different tariff headings may attract multiple While the change is aimed largely at addressing the growth of low-value e-commerce imports, it will also impact UK businesses selling products directly into EU markets, including online retailers, brands and SMEs What the new €3 EU customs duty means for UK businesses
